correctness.rationale: The full proof in RESULT.md shows at most one doubled label in a run subsequence of the two-permutation host, constructs length m+1, and counts all optimum words bijectively by record positions and independent choices of smaller later-occurring labels. Missing-smaller-element charging yields the sharp linear lower bound and consecutive singleton/adjacent-pair equality cases. Strict comparison of r*2^(m-r) yields the exponential upper bound and exactly the two prefix equality cases, with m=1 separately. The staged check.py independently exhausts all subsequence choices for every permutation of at most five symbols, and all permutations up to nine symbols for equality classes; it completed without discrepancies. Finite checking is corroborative and not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2020, 2021, 2023 and 2025 primary work analyzes hardness, exact optimization algorithms, and bounded-occurrence approximation, but does not state or imply the number of distinct optima in concatenated-permutation hosts, the weighted-record formula, or the complete two-sided equality classifications. Search of published mathematical research records and accessible prior scientific claims revealed no equivalent; the known OEIS factorial combination is only the coincident numerical sequence and has no run-subsequence implication. Residual risks include inaccessible/unindexed work and the early Japanese technical report metadata-only access.
residual_risks: The earlier Japanese technical report was available as bibliographic metadata only, whereas the full publisher paper was readable.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete counting and structural-extremal classification of how many optimal outputs exist at a tractable boundary of a known hard genome-scaffolding problem: optimum length is fixed but solution degeneracy varies sharply from m to 2^(m-1). Both equality families are characterized and exactly counted for every alphabet size, with a computable closed record statistic for every member. This is substantive mathematical structure, not merely a one-off numerical census, trivial parity check, or renamed source theorem.
